## User story

**As a** developer,
**I want** each public API success and rejection response tested,
**so that** clients can depend on the status codes and safe response contract.

Traceability: **STORY-024 → EPIC-008 → FR-24** in [requirements](../../../agile/requirements.md); FR-14 through FR-18 and NFR-7 also apply.

## Acceptance criteria

**AC1 — Successful routes**
Given all service boundaries are mocked,
when `TestClient` requests health, successful analysis and recent scans,
then each returns HTTP 200 with its documented payload and empty history returns an empty scans list.

**AC2 — Unsafe uploads**
Given unsupported content types and files exceeding the specified upload limit,
when analysis requests are submitted,
then they return HTTP 415 and HTTP 413 respectively before any cloud call; the exact byte boundary is **TBD (OQ-2)**.

**AC3 — Service failures**
Given mocked `VisionAnalysisError` and `DatabaseError`,
when affected requests run,
then the API returns HTTP 502 and HTTP 503 respectively without stack traces, project IDs, bucket names, topic paths or raw cloud payloads.

**AC4 — Identity validation**
Given empty supplied identity strings or latitude/longitude outside -90..90/-180..180,
when multipart requests run,
then they return HTTP 422, while inclusive endpoints are accepted and valid supplied identity values are preserved verbatim.

## Tasks

- [x] Provide an offline fixture guard and install `httpx`/pytest tooling in the delivered dependency baseline
- [ ] Create `TestClient` tests with all controller service boundaries mocked
- [ ] Cover HTTP 200, 413, 415, 422, 502 and 503 and empty scan history
- [ ] Assert upload rejection and identity rejection precede cloud work
- [ ] Resolve **OQ-2** for exact 10 MB bytes and plausible temperature boundaries before boundary-test acceptance
- [ ] Assert sanitized errors using deliberately sensitive fake exception messages
- [ ] Prove valid supplied identity preservation and API response fields `doc_id` and `climate_source`
- [ ] File exposed controller defects through the orchestrator rather than editing production code in the QA story

## Current state

The pytest harness is delivered, but `backend/main.py` has **0% coverage** in the verified 61.7% whole-backend baseline. Today's controller exposes health, analysis and scans, but does not await the delivered async analyzer (**BUG-007**), gates alerts on a removed field (**BUG-008**) and uses wildcard CORS (**BUG-009**). It does not yet implement the required upload/identity/error boundaries. Tests must assert the desired external contract and surface those defects, not encode today's broken responses as expected behaviour.

The older epic enumerated only 200/415/413/502/503; resolved identity requirements in FR-15 add **422** and must be covered as well. The exact upload byte limit and plausible temperature range remain **TBD (OQ-2)**. No live route tests or cloud calls were run during this document pass; STORY-024 remains blocked on EPIC-05.

## Test cases

| Test                                                 | Asserts                                                                                              |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `test_api_success_routes_and_empty_history`          | Health, analysis and scans return documented 200 payloads; empty scans stay empty                    |
| `test_api_rejects_uploads_before_cloud_calls`        | Unsupported/oversized uploads return 415/413 at the resolved byte boundary                           |
| `test_api_service_failures_are_safe`                 | Vision/database errors map to 502/503 without internal details                                       |
| `test_api_validates_and_preserves_supplied_identity` | Invalid multipart identity returns 422; inclusive valid coordinates and supplied values are retained |

## Definition of done

All four parameterised route groups pass with mocked services, every required status code is asserted, OQ-2 boundaries are resolved, no sensitive detail leaks, and controller coverage contributes to NFR-9's whole-backend floor.
